rules.rationale: Electronegative halide p states sit deep below the Fermi level, giving strongly ionic solids the widest experimental gaps.
Main-group oxides lack partially filled d bands, so conduction edges stay high and measured gaps remain wide.
Polarizable S, Se, Te p states raise the valence-band edge, systematically narrowing gaps relative to oxides and halides.
Low mean atomic number implies compact orbitals, weak spin-orbit splitting, and low polarizability, all widening band gaps.

skills.hypothesis: Target-native ionic wide-gap chemistry: electronegative closed-shell anions with light main-group cations, penalizing polarizable chalcogenides. Fails if halide and light-oxide subsets are too small or if d0 transition-metal oxides dominate the extreme top.

rules.rationale: Largest source refractive-index effect (+9.23); Moss relation implies high polarizability accompanies narrow experimental gaps.
Halogen dominance depressed source refractive index (-3.74), which under Moss inversion predicts wide ionic band gaps.
Heavy elements gave the top mean_z source effect (+6.07); larger polarizability and spin-orbit splitting shrink gaps.
Pnictides raised source refractive index (+3.97); their covalent, less ionic bonding usually yields narrow measured gaps.

skills.hypothesis: Counter-hypothesis reversing source refractive-index signs via the Moss relation while dropping near-zero-confidence lanthanide and transition-metal transfers. Fails if experimental gaps here reflect structure or reporting bias rather than composition-driven polarizability.

lesson: Source evidence is refractive index, physically anti-correlated with band gap through the Moss relation, and its per-field confidences are weak (0.006-0.37). Same-sign transfer would chase narrow-gap polarizable chemistries, so the target-native ionic wide-gap prior carries higher confidence and larger early semantic mass, while the inverted-transfer skill remains the low-confidence counter-hypothesis.
revision_summary: Corrected the schema violation: conditions are now objects mapping catalog fields directly to exact catalog values instead of list-of-lists. Kept the domain-knowledge wide-gap ionic skill but replaced the weaker transition-metal-flag rule with an explicit chalcogenide valence-edge penalty covering the largest anion subset. Trimmed the Moss-inverted transfer skill to the highest-support source signals (metalloid, halogen, mean_z_high, pnictide) and explicitly dropped the near-zero-confidence lanthanide and transition-metal transfers. All weights, ridge, prior scale, semantic masses, betas, xi, and confidences remain inside the allowed ranges; source effects were used only for sign and emphasis reasoning.
